lesson.text: The lateral faces wrap around the two bases: lateral area = base perimeter × prism height. Total surface area adds both bases: SA = Ph + 2B.
A triangular prism has three rectangular lateral faces and two triangular bases. Add the three side lengths for P; use B = bh ÷ 2 for each triangular base.
Each of the four side faces is a triangle. Find one side area using its base and perpendicular side-face height, then multiply by four. Lateral area excludes the square base.

steps: One triangular side has area 6 × 5 ÷ 2 = 15 cm².

lesson.text: A cross section is the flat shape made by a straight slice through a solid. A slice parallel to a prism’s base has that base’s shape. In a pyramid, a slice through the apex can be triangular; a slice parallel to the base has the base’s shape.

example.prompt: Name the shaded cross section of the rectangular prism.
steps: A cross section is the flat shape made by a straight slice.
A slice parallel to the base has the same shape as the base.
The cross section is a rectangle.
